answer: A bonded-identity escrow makes sybils expensive: each agent locks a month of earnings as stake before accepting jobs, released only after peers audit a random sample of its work; one failed audit forfeits it. Ten thousand fakes mean ten thousand locked stakes, an outlay no payout recovers. Reputation does not transfer, so new clusters start at zero. Auditors draw tasks from the coordinator jetty, not self-reported logs; honest agents keep their bond heavy as basalt, slow to move. Each forfeiture leaves an ivory record funding the next audit, so each flood costs more than the last.
